challenge.better_approach: Considered workflow_grammar.is_terminal, which reads the hardcoded TERMINAL_STATES. The orchestrator ruled the set must come from the class definitions, and reading the class keeps one source: the class already declares its dispositions and its path.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That every live ticket's workflow parses. Measured: 1072 of 1072 in the house commons parse with parse_workflow, and every class named resolves.
challenge.prior_art: aa3e9a70db47 built the migration with the PROVED-only selector. workflow_grammar.is_disposition reads class_def['dispositions']; transitions.load_class_def loads a class from a given root. Both are reused.
challenge.real_collision: none: the aa3e proof's scratch commons had no node_classes, so it now needs them copied in, the way a real commons carries them. Its 9 teeth stay green.

answers.falsifier: On a scratch commons with PROVED, SUPERSEDED, RETIRED and DROPPED code-seam tickets plus one at BUILDME, only the BUILDME ticket is selected and the others stay byte-identical. A scratch class's own path end is terminal while an undeclared disposition is not. An unknown class refuses the run, naming it.
answers.from_idea: none, because this was measured, not imagined: _proved in cairn/machines/rehearsal/plan_migration.py selects a ticket as open whenever its workflow lacks '[PROVED]', which picks 52 terminal tickets on the house commons
answers.how: In cairn/machines/rehearsal/plan_migration.py, replace _proved with _terminal: parse the ticket's workflow, load its class from <root>/node_classes via transitions.load_class_def, and treat the last state of each workflow version plus the class's dispositions as terminal. A class with no definition refuses the run. A red-first proof builds a scratch commons with one ticket per terminal kind plus one in flight.
answers.traces_to: Law 5: a terminal ticket is a record of what happened, and a record of truth is not rewritten. Law 1: the terminal set is read from the class, not re-derived as a hardcoded list.
answers.what: The plan migration selects only tickets still in flight: a ticket whose cursor stands at one of its class's terminals is never opened for write, the terminal set read from the class definition.

bullets.text: The plan migration's selector treated everything not PROVED as open. On the house commons that would have rewritten 52 terminal tickets (38 SUPERSEDED, 11 RETIRED, 3 DROPPED). It now reads each class's terminal set.
